title: The name in imperial service
eyebrow: 1827 to 1918 · twelve entries · none of them proved kin
dek: Ninety-one years of Habsburg paperwork, and a De Franceschi in it almost continuously — the passport desk at Fiume, the quarantine station, the port captaincy, the chamber, the navy, the army and the Landwehr. Not one of them can be attached to a household on this site. The pattern is the finding.
lede: This archive opened Hungaricana for the first time on 13 September 2026 and found, within an afternoon, more men of the name in imperial service than it had found in a year of parish registers. That is not because the men are more interesting. It is because **a state writes down the people it employs, every year, by name, and prints it.**

What follows is everything the Austrian and Hungarian service lists give. It is set out as a single roll because the individual entries are thin and the shape of them together is not: from the year the Bakar salt office was drawn to the year the monarchy ended, **there is hardly a decade without one.**

**A warning that applies to every line of it.** These lists record a man's year of birth, his service dates and his unit. **They do not record where he was born.** Not one of the eight can be attached to a household in this archive, and none is claimed as kin. They are here because they are of the name, in one empire, in one span of years — and because the next person to work on this will want the citations.

roll.detail: Drew the **«Bauriss der zu Buccari befündlichen aerarial Salz-Einnehmer und Controlors Wohnung»** — the ground plan and section of the imperial salt-receiver's and comptroller's residence at **Bakar**. Manuscript, 56 × 45 cm, one sheet.
roll.src: National Archives of Hungary, T 62 No 1642, out of E 96 Tricesimalia 1827, 4:51

roll.detail: ***Passualist*** in the **Polizey-Behörde of Fiume** — the officer who issued and checked passports in a free port. He is listed among the city's patrician office-holders: Tudorovich the tax-receiver, Bossich the comptroller, Celebrini the book-keeper and orphans' commissioner, Peretti the chief fiscal. **This is the earliest office this archive can put the name in**, and it is a civil one.
roll.src: «Der Pesther Stadt- und Landbothe für das Königreich Ungarn», 1835, Gerichtsbarkeiten, p. 71

roll.detail: ***Főnök*** — head — of the **«szent Ferenczről czimzett Martinsiczai veszteglő intézet»**, the quarantine institute at **Martinšćica** named for St Francis: the lazaretto of the Kvarner, where ships and crews were held before they were let into the ports. Under him a clerk, a surgeon-teacher, a chaplain and four guards. **On the same page the harbour captaincy at Buccari is recorded as vacant** — *Kapitány. Nincs.* — nine years before Ferencz himself is pensioned as a port captain.
In the **Marine-Direktion at Pola**. *Valentin* is the forename that runs through the Rijeka households — a Valentino fathering there in 1742–57, and another in 1794–1805.

***M. kir.* révkapitány** in the service of the **Fiume Maritime Authority** — 42 years, 10 months and 5 days of public service, pension of 1,050 forints from 1857, which puts him into state service about 1814. His port is not named; the authority governed the whole Hungarian Littoral, **Bakar included**.

A **cadet** in a line infantry regiment in 1859, an **Unterleutnant 2. Classe** in 1863 — and a **cadet again** in 1867. **That does not describe one career.** Either these are two men of the same name in two regiments, or one of the entries is wrong. This archive has not resolved it and will not guess.

On a ***kegydíj*** of **65 forints** a year, granted in three-year terms and renewed again and again — *«tekintettel vagyontalanságára, munka- és keresetképtelenségére»*, in view of her destitution and her incapacity for work or earning. Her father was dead by 1888; she was still on the list in 1900.

Born 1879. Naval academy 1894, commissioned 1 July 1898, Linienschiffsfähnrich and head of the harbour depot at Trieste by 1904, **Linienschiffsleutnant commanding a patrol boat on the Danube** by 1909, aboard the armoured cruiser *Kaiserin und Königin Maria Theresia* in 1910, at the **Marinedetachement in Budapest** in 1912, and still on the active list on 27 July 1918.
roll.src: 181 entries across 79 volumes of the navy rank lists — transcribed in full

roll.detail: Not a De Franceschi, but the family that gave this one **Lambertina Peschle**, mother of Carlo the historian. Commissioned 1 August 1895, rank from 5 September 1895; *Assistenzarzt*, then with the 5th and 23rd Regiments, attached to the **Landsturm district of Görz — Gorizia**, where Carlo had been sent to the seminary seventy years earlier.
roll.src: Schematismus der K. K. Landwehr, Wien 1896–1914; Ranglisten 1916, 1918

roll.detail: **Fähnrich (nichtaktiv)** — reserve ensign — with seniority from **1 January 1907**, in the **27th Regiment**. Still on the Landwehr rank list in 1918, by then with a mountain-rifle regiment.
roll.src: Schematismus der K. K. Landwehr, Wien 1907–1914; Ranglisten der K. K. Landwehr 1916, 1918

roll.detail: Among the **Fähnriche (Kadetten)** of an infantry regiment through the last three years of the war. **The names around his are the tell**: Mikuličić, Rusich, Petrinić, Brkljačić, Franovich, Barbiani, Turkalj — a regiment drawing its men from the Littoral and Croatia. That is a hint about where he came from and it is not evidence.
roll.src: Ranglisten des Kaiserlichen und Königlichen Heeres, Wien 1916 p. 437, 1917 p. 579, 1918 p. 287

roll.detail:
**Four months after Julius was last printed on the Emperor's active list**, the Austrian **State Chancellor** writes to the *«südslawischen Vertreter Dr. Defranceschi»* — the South Slav representative — in the quarrel over the **«Bosnian Registratur»**, the Austro-Hungarian archives being removed to the new Yugoslavia. The correspondence sits in the Haus-, Hof- und Staatsarchiv.

**Which is where this roll ends, and it ends on both sides at once.** One man of the name is still an officer of the monarchy in July. By December another is negotiating with its last chancellor on behalf of the state that replaced it.
roll.src: HHStA, Neues Politisches Archiv 397 — Staatskanzler to Dr Defranceschi, 21 December 1918

means: **Read in order, this is not a set of soldiers. It is a municipal administration.** The passport officer of Fiume in 1835; the man who drew the imperial salt office at Bakar in 1827; the director of the Kvarner quarantine station in 1848; a royal port captain pensioned in 1857 after forty-two years. **Four civil posts before a single military one**, all of them in the same forty kilometres of coast, all of them concerned with the same thing — **who and what is allowed through a port.**

**The Kvarner households stop looking like farmers.** Nine households at Rijeka and Bakar, a salt office drawn in 1827, a royal port captain pensioned in 1857, a naval officer at Pola in the 1850s and another on the Danube in 1909 — and the *Regii* written beside the name at a Bakar baptism in 1849. That is a family in the service of the state, on the water, for most of a century.

**And it explains the saints.** Nine of the twelve children born to Valentino and Ursula at Rijeka between 1794 and 1805 carry *Nepomucena* or *Nepomuc*. John of Nepomuk is the patron invoked **against drowning** — the saint of bridges and of men whose work is on the water. In a port official's household that is not only dynastic piety.

**The 1859 pair is the sharpest thing on this page.** In that year — Magenta, Solferino, the loss of Lombardy — **Eduard Defranceschi enters the Austrian army as a cadet**, and **Valente Defranceschi abandons his desk in the Zadar accounting office and takes employment with the Italian government.** Two men of one name, one empire, one year, opposite directions. Nothing connects them. They did not need to be related for that to be the truth about the name.

**And there is a chaplain on the 1848 page worth noticing.** The quarantine staff under Ferencz Defranceschi included *«Káplán. Kobler Kajetán»*. **Kobler** is the name of the Rijeka historian **Giovanni Kobler**, whose correspondence with Carlo De Franceschi this archive holds and leans on. Two names that this site already keeps in one folder, standing in one lazaretto on the Kvarner in 1848. It proves nothing whatever. It is exactly the kind of coincidence that turns out to be a small world rather than a connection — and it is written down so that nobody has to find it twice.
cannot: **No birthplaces.** The service lists give a year of birth and nothing about where. Every man on this page is unplaced, and that is the single thing that would turn the roll into genealogy.
**No deaths after 1918.** The trail ends with the monarchy. Austrian, Hungarian and Croatian records of the republics have not been searched for any of them.
**And two identities unresolved**: whether Eduard is one man or two, and whether the Alexander Peschle of 1797 and the Alexander of 1803 are brothers, cousins, or an index splitting one man.

**The document that would break all of it open is the same in every case.** Habsburg officer personnel files — *Grundbuchblätter* — are at the **Kriegsarchiv in Vienna**, are arranged by regiment, and carry birthplace, parents, religion and marriage. They are not digitised and must be asked for by name and unit. This page now holds the units.

**And a new name with no first name at all.** The South Slav representative of December 1918 is given only as *Dr Defranceschi*. Who he was, and whether he is the Zadar branch, the Kvarner one or neither, is unknown — but the file that would say is catalogued: **HHStA, Neues Politisches Archiv 397**.
